questions.subject: MATH
questions.learningObjective: Solve problems involving logic circuits and truth tables.
questions.stem: For this problem, a combinational circuit has 8 two-valued inputs and one output. Exactly how many rows are in its truth chart?

options.misconception: Wrong belief "squares the input count" gives 64, not 256.
Wrong belief "doubles rather than exponentiates" gives 16, not 256.
Wrong belief "omits one input combination" gives 255, not 256.

questions.explanation: With 8 binary inputs there are 2 to the power 8 distinct input combinations, so the truth table has 256 rows.
questions.hint: Each input doubles the number of rows.

questions.subject: MATH
questions.learningObjective: Solve problems involving logic circuits and truth tables.
questions.stem: Under this scenario, a circuit is built from 8 two-input AND gates, each fed by separate external wires. Altogether how many external input wires are required?

options.misconception: Wrong belief "counts gates instead of their input wires" gives 8, not 16.
Wrong belief "squares the gate count" gives 64, not 16.
Wrong belief "adds two wires regardless of gate count" gives 10, not 16.

questions.explanation: Each of the 8 gates needs two input wires and no wires are shared, so the circuit requires 16 external inputs.
questions.hint: Two input wires per gate, all distinct.

questions.stem: Under this scenario, a Karnaugh map for a Logical function of 3 variables has altogether how many cells?

questions.stem: A Boolean function of 7 variables is true on 126 assignments. How many cells of its Karnaugh map contain a zero?

questions.hint: Subtract the one-cells from the total cell count.
